newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION - Blues prepare for French intensity.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Blues prepare for French intensity.

text.p: LONDON, Feb 20 - Auckland Blues are preparing themselves for the passion and intensity that only French rugby supporters can bring to a match, when they play Brive on Saturday.
Auckland arrived in the southern French town yesterday to find themselves at the centre of what is looming as one of the town's most important occasions.
Brive won the European Cup title last month, and are not holding back in promoting their clash with Auckland as the world club championship.

The emotion that is attached to the match, with the town of 50,000's pride at stake, will turn itself into an intense atmosphere on Saturday that even some of Auckland's most battle-hardened players have not seen.
"The mood here is just incredible," Blues coach Graham Henry told NZPA.
"They think it's the world championship of club rugby, which I suppose they can do. For them if they win they're the world champions, but if they lose it's just a friendly.
"It will be an amazing atmosphere, and something for the players to remember.
"They're going to have roosters and bands on the field, firecrackers, the whole works.
"The stadium fits about 18,000 but that's about a third of the population of the town. It's a huge occasion for them."
Auckland will take the field with their strongest possible side for a match that forms the final leg of their European mini-tour before they travel to South Africa for two Super 12 matches.

They include injured duo Dylan Mika (groin) and Carlos Spencer (broken finger), in a team that boasts 13 internationals. Only prop Paul Thomson and flanker Charles Riechelmann have yet to represent their country.
Henry said Spencer's injury, sustained in the 33-29 win over Harlequins on Tuesday, was a relatively minor broken bone in his little finger.

For Mika, the Western Samoan now serving a stand-down period to qualify for New Zealand, the match is his first on tour after picking up his adductor muscle injury in training before the match in Bristol.
He will pack down at No 8, with the versatile Riechelmann switching to the blindside flank.
"He's probably not 100 percent but we have to give him a game," Henry added.
"It's important that he plays, because it's our last match before going to South Africa."
Henry is happy at the Blues' progress on the pre-season tour, but he will be asking for more commitment from his players than that shown in the lucky win over Harlequins.
"It's important that we go up a couple of notches for this one," Henry said.
"It's hard for the players to go into this pre-season stuff, but we need to be going at about 85 percent now.
"But you can't put too much acid on at this stage."

Brive, like Auckland, are expected to field their strongest possible side, including French test players Christophe Lamaison and David Venditti, while halfback Philippe Carbonneau is expected to be fit. New Zealander Grant Ross, a lock from Wellington, is also expected to play.

Auckland Blues: Adrian Cashmore, Joeli Vidiri, Eroni Clarke, Brian Lima, Lee Stensness, Carlos Spencer, Junior Tonu'u, Dylan Mika, Mark Carter, Robin Brooke, Richard Fromont, Charles Riechelmann, Paul Thomson, Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), Olo Brown.
